plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic drawing of a polarimeter, laid out as a single optical path running left to right in perspective. At the far left a lit incandescent bulb sits in a socket inside a yellow glow, labeled "Light source", and short red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions emerge from it beneath the label "Unpolarized light". The beam is drawn as a flat pale yellow ribbon that passes through a circular disc with fine vertical striping, labeled "Polarizer", after which the red arrows all lie in a single vertical plane under the label "Polarized light". The ribbon then runs through a horizontal cylinder with a small filling stub on top, drawn with rounded ends and labeled "Sample tube containing organic molecules"; the red arrows inside progressively tip away from vertical as they move along the tube. Beyond the tube the beam meets a second striped disc labeled "Analyzer" and continues to the right, where a heavy red double-headed arrow lies at a slant. A vertical dashed reference line and a curved arrow mark the angle between the two, labeled with the Greek letter alpha, and a drawn eye at the right edge is labeled "Observer". Tracking one ribbon of light through every component makes the tilt of the arrows the quantity to follow. The arrangement shows how the rotation an optically active sample imposes on the plane of polarization is measured.

interactions.label: Analyzer rotation α
interactions.teaches: Rotating the analyzer changes the plane it transmits and the measured angle α; maximum transmission occurs when the analyzer is aligned with the sample-rotated polarization plane

interactions.label: Sample optical activity
interactions.teaches: An optically active sample rotates plane-polarized light gradually as it travels through the tube; the sign and size of the rotation determine the final polarization angle before the analyzer

interactions.label: Send light pulse
interactions.teaches: Following a pulse from left to right shows each component's role: the source emits many polarization directions, the polarizer selects one plane, the sample rotates that plane, and the analyzer tests the resulting angle

demo_steps.title: No optical rotation
demo_steps.narration: With optical activity set to 0°, the arrows after the polarizer remain vertical throughout the sample tube. The analyzer is also vertical when α=0°, so it is aligned with the unchanged polarization plane.

demo_steps.title: Sample rotates the plane
demo_steps.narration: Set the sample to +30°. The red arrows inside the tube twist progressively, ending at a +30° tilted plane before the analyzer.

demo_steps.title: Analyzer finds α
demo_steps.narration: Rotate the analyzer to +30°. Its stripes and outgoing red arrow now match the final polarization plane, so the measured angle α equals the sample-imposed rotation.

demo_steps.title: Opposite optical activity
demo_steps.narration: A negative optical activity twists the arrows the other way. The analyzer must be rotated to the same negative angle to recover maximum transmission.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use +X as the optical path from left to right, +Y vertical on screen, and +Z depth. Overall apparatus spans about X=-4.4 to +4.8, Y=-1.2 to +1.4, Z=-0.7 to +0.7. Light source centered near x=-3.8: socket is a short white/gray cylinder radius 0.35, height 0.18, oriented vertically; bulb is a transparent warm glass sphere/teardrop about 0.55 high with yellow emissive glow radius about 1.0 behind it. Unpolarized arrows occupy a loose disk centered at x=-3.1, y=0.35, z=0, each length about 0.35, colored red #e31b23, with orientations 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150° in the local YZ plane. Beam is a pale translucent yellow ribbon/cylinder along +X, color #e8c36b, radius/half-height about 0.18 near the source and 0.22 through the tube; keep it mostly flat like the source drawing. Polarizer at x=-2.35, vertical disc normal to +X, radius 0.55, thickness 0.16, dark rim #555555; face is tan/green #b6c987 with many thin vertical stripe lines parallel to +Y, showing its transmission axis vertical. Sample tube runs from x=-1.55 to x=1.35, radius 0.42, transparent pale cyan #bfe6e6 at 35% opacity, with rounded caps and a small top stub centered at x=0.0, y=0.48, radius 0.12, height 0.28. Place 5 red double-headed arrows inside the tube at evenly spaced x positions from -1.25 to +1.15; their angle about the X-axis is theta(x)=sampleOpticalActivity*((x+1.25)/(2.4)), measured from vertical +Y toward screen-down/right slant as positive in the source view. Analyzer at x=2.65, disc radius 0.55, thickness 0.16, dark gray rim #555555; its stripe/pass-axis orientation rotates by analyzerAngle about the X-axis, using 0° as vertical. Outgoing heavy red double-headed arrow centered near x=3.85, length 0.9, angle analyzerAngle about the X-axis. Show a fainter incoming final-polarization arrow just before the analyzer at angle sampleOpticalActivity if helpful. Alpha arc is drawn in the observer-side plane near x=4.05, from vertical dashed reference to analyzerAngle, radius about 0.55, black #222222, labeled α. Vertical dashed reference line extends y=-0.5 to y=0.8 near x=4.0. Eye sits at x=4.65, y=-0.05, stylized tan/black. Dominant colors: beam #e8c36b, red arrows #e31b23, glow #f2f36b with soft opacity, glass tube #bfe6e6, metal rims #555555, labels black. Analyzer transmission intensity may be represented by outgoing beam opacity proportional to cos²((analyzerAngle - sampleOpticalActivity) in radians), with a low minimum opacity so the beam remains visible for teaching.
interactionPlan.notes: Build all polarization arrows as double-headed arrow helpers or thin cylinders with cone heads at both ends, oriented in the local YZ plane while their centers advance along X. The light-pulse animation should move a small bright yellow packet along the beam from source to observer; when the packet is before the polarizer, briefly show multiple red orientations, between polarizer and tube show vertical only, inside tube interpolate continuously to sampleOpticalActivity, and after analyzer show analyzerAngle with opacity/intensity tied to Malus' law. Use billboarded text labels matching the original positions: labels above the source and post-polarizer beam, labels below the light source, polarizer, tube, analyzer, and observer. Keep orbit disabled by default or absent so the left-to-right textbook composition remains recognizable.

authoredContext:
The angle of rotation can be measured with an instrument called a polarimeter, represented in the figure. A solution of optically active organic molecules is placed in a sample tube, plane-polarized light is passed through the tube, and rotation of the polarization plane occurs. The light then goes through a second polarizer called the analyzer. By rotating the analyzer until the light passes through it, we can find the new plane of polarization and can tell to what extent rotation has occurred.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Plane-polarized light passes through a solution of optically active molecules, which rotate the plane of polarization.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Unpolarized light from light source passes through polarizer, followed by polarized light, sample tube containing organic molecules, analyzer, and observer.

In addition to determining the extent of rotation, we can also find the direction. From the vantage point of the observer looking directly at the analyzer, some optically active molecules rotate polarized light to the left (counterclockwise) and are said to be levorotatory, whereas others rotate polarized light to the right (clockwise) and are said to be dextrorotatory. By convention, rotation to the left is given a minus sign (−) and rotation to the right is given a plus sign (+). (−)-Morphine, for example, is levorotatory, and (+)-sucrose is dextrorotatory.

interactions.label: Analyzer rotation α
interactions.teaches: Rotating the analyzer changes the plane it transmits and the measured angle α; maximum transmission occurs when the analyzer is aligned with the sample-rotated polarization plane

interactions.label: Sample optical activity
interactions.teaches: An optically active sample rotates plane-polarized light gradually as it travels through the tube; the sign and size of the rotation determine the final polarization angle before the analyzer

interactions.label: Send light pulse
interactions.teaches: Following a pulse from left to right shows each component's role: the source emits many polarization directions, the polarizer selects one plane, the sample rotates that plane, and the analyzer tests the resulting angle

demo_steps.title: No optical rotation
demo_steps.narration: With optical activity set to 0°, the arrows after the polarizer remain vertical throughout the sample tube. The analyzer is also vertical when α=0°, so it is aligned with the unchanged polarization plane.

demo_steps.title: Sample rotates the plane
demo_steps.narration: Set the sample to +30°. The red arrows inside the tube twist progressively, ending at a +30° tilted plane before the analyzer.

demo_steps.title: Analyzer finds α
demo_steps.narration: Rotate the analyzer to +30°. Its stripes and outgoing red arrow now match the final polarization plane, so the measured angle α equals the sample-imposed rotation.

demo_steps.title: Opposite optical activity
demo_steps.narration: A negative optical activity twists the arrows the other way. The analyzer must be rotated to the same negative angle to recover maximum transmission.
